title: Standing Order
description: One standing order (SO): a commander order promoted to permanent, universal conduct, applicable across any session rather than the one it was given in. Filed in records/commander/orders/ beside the COs, with rows in the same manifest; the CO it was promoted from becomes superseded and is never pruned. SO numbering is its own sequence, separate from CO's. Retired and eventually pruned if it stops applying. Filed by identifier with a dash, SO-004.json.

kind.description: the word standing-order, which is what chooses this schema

id.description: this standing order's identifier, SO, a dash and three digits, the same identifier the file is named for

name.description: one to three words the writer chose for the record's contents, appended to the file name after the id (CA-049)

date.description: the day it was promoted to standing, YYYY-MM-DD

session.description: the eight-character id of the session that promoted it

status.description: whether the standing order still holds: active while it governs conduct, retired once it stops applying

summary.description: a plain-language summary of the whole order, simple words with no jargon; only this text goes to the manifest

statement.description: the commander's own words, verbatim and never edited

brief.description: the surrounding context: why the order was found to be universal conduct rather than a single session's

from.description: the CO this standing order was promoted from; that CO becomes superseded on promotion and is never pruned

superseded_by.description: the identifier of the later standing order that overrides this one, and nothing else; absent while it stands

superseded_note.description: how and why it was superseded, in prose, when the identifier alone does not tell the story
